questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds, on reaction with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaOH</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> gives yellow colour?
questions.solution:
Chromium hydroxide, i.e.CrOH3 when reacts with NaOH and Na2O2, gives yellow colour of sodium chromate. The whole reaction is as follows

3Na2O2+2CrOH3⟶2Na2CrO4(yellow)+2H2O+2NaOH

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math> gas is passed into a mixture of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Mn</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Ni</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Cu</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Hg</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ion in an acidified aqueous solution, the precipitates formed are
questions.solution:
In presence of acidic medium, ionisation of H2S is supressed so less number of S2- ions are produced. So only those sulphides are precipitated which have low solubility product Ksp value.

Thus, in acidic medium, H2S is very feebly ionised giving very small concentration of sulphide ion for precipitation. Therefore, the most insoluble salts CuS and HgS are precipitated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sometimes, the colour observed in Lassaigne's test for nitrogen is green. It is because
options: of green colour of ferrous sulphate
of green colour of copper sulphate
of excess of Fe $^{3+}$ ions whose yellow colour makes the blue colour of ferric ferrocyanide to appear green.
questions.solution: Although blue coloured ferric ferrocyanide is formed but due to the presence of yellow coloured $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ salts, the blue colour gives the shade of green.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A mixture of chlorides of copper, cadmium, chromium, iron and aluminium was dissolved in water acidified with $\mathrm{HCl}$ and hydrogen sulphide gas was passed for sufficient time. It was filtered, boiled and a few drops of nitric acid were added while boiling. To this solution ammonium chloride and sodium hydroxide were added and filtered. The filterate shall give test for.
questions.solution: CuS and CdS are precipitated by $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$. Hydroxide of Al will pass into the solution in the form of $\mathrm{NaAlO}_{2}$ being amphoteric in nature. Hence filtrate will give test for sodium and aluminium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ gas when passed through a solution of cations containing $\mathrm{HCl}$ precipitates the cations of second group of qualitative analysis but not those belonging to the fourth group. It is because
options: presence of HC1 decreases the sulphide ion concentration.
solubility product of group II sulphides is more than that of group IV sulphides.
presence of HCl increases the sulphide ion concentration.
sulphides of group IV cations are unstable in $\mathrm{HC} 1$
questions.solution: IV $^{\text {th }}$ group needs higher $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ ion concentration. In presence of $\mathrm{HCl}$, the dissociation of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ decreases hence produces less amount of sulphide ions due to common ion effect, thus $\mathrm{HCl}$ decreases the solubility of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ which is sufficient to precipitate II $^{\text {nd }}$ group radicals.
